2609.08558.title: Personalizing LLM Agent Memory Using Biometrics
2609.08558.paper_summary: Personalized memory helps LLM agents deliver stable, tailored assistance by storing and reusing user-specific data across interactions. In multi-user scenarios, however, retrieval must consider not only semantic similarity but also whether the current requester matches the identity associated with the stored memory. We propose Bio-Memory, a biometric-aware memory architecture that conditions memory retrieval on both semantic similarity and biometric matching. Built on top of A-Mem, Bio-Memory augments each atomic memory note with a biometric embedding and uses biometric matching to form the retrieval candidate pool before semantic ranking. We evaluate Bio-Memory on LoCoMo in a 10-user shared-agent setting over 7 face benchmarks and 10 palmprint protocols. Across datasets, Bio-Memory consistently separates owner and non-owner queries. Under face-based personalization, the largest average gap reaches 27.29% / 21.15% in F1 / BLEU-1 on CALFW; under palmprint-based personalization, the corresponding gap is 25.75% / 19.22% on MS_Blue. These results support biometrics as a practical control signal for personalized memory retrieval in shared environments.
2609.08558.paper_summary_zh: 個性化記憶幫助大型語言模型代理提供穩定且量身定制的協助，通過在互動中存儲和重用用戶特定數據。然而，在多用戶場景中，檢索必須考慮的不僅是語義相似性，還有當前請求者是否與存儲的記憶相關聯的身份匹配。我們提出了生物記憶（Bio-Memory），這是一種生物識別感知的記憶架構，將記憶檢索條件化為語義相似性和生物識別匹配。生物記憶基於A-Mem構建，為每個原子記憶筆記增強了生物識別嵌入，並在語義排名之前使用生物識別匹配形成檢索候選池。我們在LoCoMo上對生物記憶進行評估，在10用戶共享代理設置中，涵蓋7個面部基準和10個掌紋協議。在各個數據集上，生物記憶始終能夠區分擁有者和非擁有者的查詢。在基於面部的個性化中，最大的平均差距在CALFW上達到27.29% / 21.15% 的F1 / BLEU-1；在基於掌紋的個性化中，相應的差距在MS_Blue上為25.75% / 19.22%。這些結果支持生物識別作為共享環境中個性化記憶檢索的實用控制信號。
